title: Formulation, Characterization, and Preliminary Stability of a Topical Ointment Containing a Kratom-Based Polyherbal Extract
content: Background/Objectives: Thai Herbal Kratom recipe (THK) is a traditional polyherbal formulation used for muscle pain relief, traditionally administered as a herbal compress ball. However, its conventional dosage form has limitations in terms of convenience, reproducibility, and stability. This study aimed to pharmaceutically formulate THK into a stable topical ointment and evaluate its physicochemical properties and changes in total phenolic content (TPC) and total flavonoid content (TFC) during storage. Methods: Five ointment formulations (THK-F1–THK-F5) containing 0.2% (w/w) THK extract were prepared and evaluated for physicochemical characteristics. The selected formulation, THK-F3, was profiled using LC-QTOF-MS/MS. The physicochemical stability of THK-F3 and its corresponding extract-free base (B-F3) was compared through heating–cooling cycle testing and storage at 4 °C and 30 °C for 180 days. TPC and TFC were monitored during storage to evaluate changes in phytochemical content. Results: THK-F3 showed acceptable physicochemical characteristics. Chemical profiling tentatively identified 99 compounds, including mitragynine and several phenolic compounds. Phase separation occurred at 4 °C, and slight oil separation was observed after heating–cooling cycles, whereas no noticeable changes in appearance or odor occurred during storage at 30 °C. After 180 days, TPC and TFC decreased by 33.7% and 42.6%, respectively, at 30 °C, compared with 72.5% and 72.6% decreases at 4 °C. Conclusions: THK-F3 showed potential as a topical herbal formulation for further pharmaceutical development, while appropriate storage conditions are important for maintaining product quality.
